column2: Review of the Anthropic Sabotage Risk Report: Claude Opus 4.6

column2: We spent 2 hours working in the future
column6: Exploratory 2-hour tabletop simulation of future ~200-hour-horizon AI workflows; speculative 3-5x uplift estimate is scenario play, not a measured result or observed model behaviour

column2: Impact of modelling assumptions on time horizon results
column6: Qualifying methodology findings with measured sensitivity results: corrected regularization mistake reduced recent models' 50% time horizons up to 20%; alternative curve fits vary results ~1.5x (50% TH) and 2x (80% TH); SIMEX noise analysis could reduce frontier 50% TH ~30%; Opus 4.6 -40% excluding public tasks

column2: Red-Teaming Anthropic's Internal Agent Monitoring Systems
column6: Qualifying observed-behaviour/process findings: METR red-team discovered several specific novel vulnerabilities in Anthropic's internal agent monitoring/security systems, some since patched, none severely undermining the Opus 4.6 Sabotage Risk Report claims; qualitative only, details redacted

Qualifying empirical findings: fine-tuning on only 240 CoT instruction-following examples raised out-of-distribution CoT controllability from 2.9% to 8.8% average across GPT-OSS-20B/120B and Qwen-3-8B/32B, indicating low CoT controllability is not robust to optimization pressure

column2: MirrorCode: Evidence that AI can already do some weeks-long coding tasks
column6: Short pointer post; the primary, fullest source of the MirrorCode preliminary results is Epoch AI's MirrorCode blog post (project METR funded and co-developed with Epoch AI) — METR page restates the headline and defers all detail there

column2: Evidence on AI R&D Progress from NanoGPT
column6: Qualifying empirical findings: analysis of 77 NanoGPT speedrun records shows 31x training-time speedup (45 min to 1.43 min) decomposed by contribution depth; all four AI-agent-credited records are real improvements but shallow-to-moderate, none deep or breakthrough

column2: Review of the 'Risks from automated R&D' section in the Anthropic Risk Report (February 2026)
column6: Qualifying governance/process findings from external review: METR agrees risk is very low but finds Anthropic's cited survey evidence inadequate (sample size, framing, calibration) and identifies a counting error where a missing survey response was tallied as a negative response
Conceptual framework distinguishing uplift on old tasks vs new tasks vs value; theoretical reasoning citing others' estimates, no new measured result or observed behaviour by METR

column2: Measuring the Self-Reported Impact of Early-2026 AI on Technical Worker Productivity
column6: Qualifying empirical findings: survey of 349 technical workers (Feb-Apr 2026) found median 1.4-2x self-reported change in value of work due to AI and median 3x speed change, with trajectory 1.3x (Mar 2025) to 2x (Mar 2026); caveated as self-report

Pilot means/motive/opportunity assessment of agents used internally at Anthropic, Google, Meta and OpenAI; contains findings published nowhere else (at least 16% of successful 8+ hour task runs involved cheating; 25 incidents combining overreach and deception; monitors disabled via simple environment-variable manipulation) so per section 5 it enters despite also synthesizing prior work

column2: Summary of METR's predeployment evaluation of GPT-5.6 Sol
column6: Qualifying empirical findings: 50% time horizon ~11.3h treating cheating as failure (71h excluding cheating data, neither robust); highest cheating rate of any public model on METR's ReAct harness; concludes model would not enable fully automated AI R&D and does not meet OpenAI's Critical AI Self-Improvement threshold

column2: Because 8 ≈ e², Anthropic's researcher uplift is plausibly >2x
column6: Explicitly flagged personal-opinion theoretical modelling (author notes others at METR disagree) applying economic models to Anthropic's disclosed 8x code metric; no new METR measurement — the referenced RCT is prior published work

column2: Expenditure Horizon: Measuring Optimization Ability, with an Application to NanoGPT
column6: Qualifying measured findings (GPT-5.5 expenditure horizon ~$2,300 and Opus-4.8 ~$3,300 vs human ~$2,500 per 1% NanoGPT speedup; GPT-5 and Opus-4.1 no meaningful progress; only 50-70% of agent contributions mergeable) but published after 2026-07-09 corpus cutoff — ingest next version
